storyboard.ears: It costs more to make than it's worth — so they're done.
Making pennies loses taxpayers about 86 million dollars a year. Ending it saves roughly two thirds of that.
storyboard.evidence: United States Mint | US penny program: annual loss vs projected savings from ending it | https://www.usmint.gov/about/congressional-reports/annual-report | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: Most dead coins went fast; the two-cent piece lasted just 9 years. The penny hung on for over two centuries.
storyboard.evidence: United States Mint | Years in production before discontinued, selected US coins | https://www.usmint.gov/ | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: A nickel costs 13.78 cents to make, nearly three times its five-cent value. The penny wasn't even the worst.
storyboard.evidence: United States Mint | Cost to produce one penny vs one nickel, 2024 | https://www.usmint.gov/about/congressional-reports/annual-report | 2026-11-13

storyboard.ears: The nickel loses even more money, so your pocket change may be next.
